d56: One-half plus one-third equals two-fifths. Is that right? Pause and spot the mistake. Adding denominators changes the size of the pieces. Instead, use sixths. One-half is three sixths. One-third is two sixths. Add those equal pieces: five sixths. Try one-quarter plus one-half. The answer is three-quarters. Same unit size, then add the pieces.
d57: Can you name this country from its shape? Clue one: an archipelago on the western edge of the Pacific. Clue two: its neighbors include Korea, China and Russia. Final clue: its capital is Tokyo. It’s Japan. Which clue gave it away? The outline, the location, or the capital?
d59: What causes the seasons: distance from the Sun, or Earth’s tilt? The tilt is the key. Earth’s axis is tilted about twenty-three and a half degrees. When the northern hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight and longer days. Six months later, it tilts away. The hemispheres have opposite seasons. The diagrams show the mechanism, not the true scale.
d60: Six times seven. Here are six rows, with seven blocks in each. First method: split six into five plus one. Five rows give thirty-five. One more row gives seven. That makes forty-two. Second method: double three times seven. Twenty-one plus twenty-one is also forty-two. Same product, two ways to see it. Choose the method you can explain.
